Karthik / Marissa,

Confirming our standard position: when a customer is a Controller and Redwood is acting as a Processor, we accept and will execute the 2021 SCCs under Module 2 (Controller -> Processor). Rationale: Redwood processes per-customer instructions and does not determine purposes/means; therefore Module 2 is the appropriate module.

For EU -> UK transfers we apply the UK Addendum (UK version of the SCCs). The UK Addendum maps to the same Module 2 semantics (Controller -> Processor). There is no need to switch to Module 4 unless we were transferring personal data onward to another Processor and that recipient required a Processor->Processor legal basis. In short:
- Primary: Module 2 (C -> P) for EU->US/third country/data center flows where Redwood is Processor.
- UK: Module 2 + UK Addendum.
- Onward transfers to subprocessors: we remain Processor and rely on SCCs' applicable clauses; we also obtain subprocessors' commitments via contracts. If Auroria needs explicit Module 4 language for a specific subprocessor relationship, flag the party and we can evaluate.

I'll also note operational evidence to include: current SOC 2 Type II (report), the proposed Redwood DPA (v3.1) with SCC Annex, and an exported subprocessor roster (csv). We should redline any customer-specific addenda only if they change security/remediation obligations.

Jonas Weber
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

Hi Daniela — thanks for the note and for moving quickly. Answers below and attached evidence.

1) SCC module: Redwood will execute the 2021 SCCs under Module 2 (Controller -> Processor). Rationale: Auroria acts as Controller and Redwood handles processing per Auroria's instructions; Module 2 is the standard processor flow.

2) UK transfers: We apply the UK Addendum for transfers to the UK. The UK Addendum maps to the same Module 2 semantics (Controller -> Processor) for our relationship. If you prefer explicit UK language in the DPA, Marissa has included the recommended clause in the attached DPA v3.1.

3) Evidence attached: SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2026.pdf (redacted), Redwood_DPA_v3.1.pdf, redwood_subprocessors_202610.csv.

4) Onward transfers & subprocessors: Our current subprocessors are listed in the CSV (GCP — eu-west1 for EU-hosted instances, S3 provider for object storage, a monitoring vendor). We will notify customers per the DPA for new subprocessors and maintain subprocessors' binding terms. If Auroria has a specific subprocessor they want to review more closely, please tell us which one and we'll provide more detailed evidence (certifications, subprocessors' DPA excerpts).

5) Next steps: We prepared a DocuSign envelope for the DPA + SCCs. Execute here if that works: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/ABC123-Redwood-SCCS.

Attachments: SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2026.pdf (redacted), Redwood_DPA_v3.1.pdf, redwood_subprocessors_202610.csv
